source.title: Explorations of Self-Repair in Language Models

page_placements.theme: Graded, dose-dependent counter-response: downstream responses scale with the upstream write, so removing the write looks like compensation

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests head-level self-repair by comparing direct effects with changes in correct-token logits after resample ablation. This is a conceptual reproduction and extension of prior layer-ablation work, using individual heads and a broad pretraining distribution.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own head-ablation and mechanism results. It also discusses or cites prior findings, including backup heads and Copy Suppression; those cited findings are not recorded as results of this study. Exact per-head values in several figures are not stated in the text.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own head-level resample-ablation results on The Pile across Pythia, GPT-2 and Llama-7B. It also measures LayerNorm and neuron mechanisms. It is, however, one of the listed original sources (arXiv:2402.15390) for V3–V7, so no verdict labels are given. The tranche is relative to the Hydra-effect original: individual heads instead of layers.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors add that LayerNorm self-repair may be a side effect of taking the model off-distribution rather than intentional repair. They advise avoiding zero ablation or freezing LayerNorm. They also note that imperfect repair reduces concern for circuit discovery, because importance is heavy-tailed.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses resample ablation and compares direct effects with correct-token logit changes, but focuses on individual attention heads across pretraining data rather than the earlier work's layer ablations on narrower distributions. It also investigates LayerNorm and neuron-level mechanisms.
record.method_sensitivity: Self-repair varies substantially by prompt and head. The LayerNorm contribution depends on the ablation method; the reported fraction also depends materially on filtering to high-direct-effect tokens and clipping per-token fractions.

fits_no_version.finding: Amplifying a head's output back into its input residual stream reduces that head's direct effect (GPT2-Medium L21H1). The reduction scales with the amplification factor.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some attention heads self-repress in response to their own output signal, consistent with iterative inference.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 235 (2024)
record.problems: The main measure is correct next-token direct effect and logit change, not general task performance or the full output distribution. Several results are shown in figures without exact numerical values. Some mechanism estimates use selected heads and top-2% token filtering; the authors say the approximately 30% LayerNorm estimate is directional and sensitive to post-processing.
record.rows_left_out: Individual head points in Figures 1–3 and 20–22, and detailed neuron rankings in Figures 8 and 12–15, were not separately extracted because the plotted values are not stated numerically and would produce many figure-only rows. The reported aggregate trends and selected text-quantified examples are included.

untested.parts: No single attention-layer ablation; heads only.
The study looks at MLP erasure of the correct-token direct effect, not downregulation of the maximum-likelihood token, and does not test whether that erasure shrinks under earlier ablation.
Backup heads and copy-suppression heads are cited or discussed, not measured.
Argued in discussion (Section 5.1) only; no measured misstatement of attribution scores.
There is no systematic comparison of the amount of self-repair under mean or resample versus zero ablation. The main results use resample ablation only.

missing.what: About 60% of final-layer neurons show negligible direct-effect change and about 40% show small, cancelling changes. Sparse anti-erasure is only part of MLP self-repair.
Measured 'self-repair' sometimes far exceeds the original direct effect (overcorrection), and sometimes is far less.
Anecdotally, previous-token and induction heads do not seem to be self-repaired.
Zero ablation does not always change LayerNorm scaling more than other ablations: GPT2-Small L11H11 shows similar ratios across ablation types, while L11H3 shows a more extreme zero-ablation effect.
Per-model LayerNorm self-repair in logits by layer, showing a significant effect in later layers.

record.verdict_notes: This paper is itself an original source for the claim (V3–V7), so no verdict labels are assigned. The text names the Figure 5 head inconsistently (L11H10 in prose, L11H0 in the figure).

versions.untested_parts: The study focuses on individual attention heads, not ablating one attention layer and testing whether later attention layers restore the output.

The study examines MLP erasure and anti-erasure in correct-token direct effects, but does not test whether late MLP layers downregulate the maximum-likelihood token or whether that erasure shrinks when earlier components are ablated.
The measure is the correct next-token logit, not the full output distribution. The study does not establish uniform results across every model family or size.
Prompt-level variability and overcorrection are examined in selected settings, not systematically across all models and prompts.
The study measures final LayerNorm scaling and MLP anti-erasure neurons. It does not test backup heads or Copy-Suppression heads as mechanisms in its own experiments.
Mean, resample, and zero ablations are compared in selected LayerNorm experiments; the study does not compare all three methods across all models and heads.
The study discusses implications for ablation-based importance and circuit analysis, but does not evaluate a catalog of importance scores against an independent ground truth.

relation.reason: It reports its own head-ablation, LayerNorm and neuron experiments bearing directly on self-repair.

tranche.reason: The paper tests compensation with individual-head interventions and a related direct-effect/logit measure, differing from the earlier layer-level method.
